title: She can make herself small enough to go underground
question: R makes her 2x3 — the size an ant's tunnels actually clear. Small, most of a colony's nest is walkable; at her own height none of it is, not one cell. Two things to judge: does the change read at all when she is this small, and is the sprite the next thing you want?
context_md:
Step 2 of the held-world plan, in your order: *shrink and walk the nests*.

**Measured before it was built.** `burrow_probe arms=colony box=2x3`, 12 seeds at frame 8,000: a 2x3 body reaches **54–92%** of the roofed void a colony digs, and on **11 of 12** seeds the largest single region *is* that whole reach — one connected run, not a scatter of pockets. The same probe at `box=7x14`, her own size, reads **0% at every sample on every seed**.

**The caves turned out to be the bigger prize.** `cave_probe box=2x3` reads **99% median** over 16 seeds x 8 presets — shrinking opens the geology far more than it opens the ant nests.

**The sprite is unchanged here and that is deliberate.** The authored 7x14 art is too sparse to resample — at 2x3 it is a coloured speck, and no scaling of that table is legible. It needs drawing rather than scaling, which is judge-by-eye work and its own change.

Both frames: the real app, zoom 4, same world, one binary.

items.label: Small
items.caption: 2x3 — SMALL latched, and she is the speck on the skyline

meta.growing back: refused where there is no room
